case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated July 14,2004 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3846 of 1996)
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin J: This petition for leave to appeal has been filed against the judgment dated July 14, 2004 of Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3846 of 1996 discharging the Rule obtained against the judgment and decree dated August 29, 1995 of the Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) and Artha Rin Adalat, Sylhet in Title Appeal No. 9 of 1995 affirming the judgment and decree dated November 30, 1994 of the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Balaganj, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 33 of 1993 decreeing the suit.

<u>2. The suit was for declaration of title by adverse possession and for further declaration that the kabala bearing No. 10146 dated March 17, 1983, the kabala bearing No. 19698 dated March 28, 1983 and the kabala bearing No. 16758 dated 13.12.1989 are void, collusive and fraudulent.</u>

3. The suit was filed stating, inter alia, that the land in suit belonged to Manada Chandra Ghosh. He borrowed Tk. 1,000/- from Nagesh Chandra Ghosh and as security Manada Chandra Ghosh executed 2 kabalas on August 1, 1962 and August 3, 1962 in favour of Nagesh Chandra Ghosh and on August 14, 1962 Nagesh Chandra Ghosh executed and registered an Ekrarnama in favour of Manada Chandra Ghosh to the effect that if the borrowed money is returned within two years, Nagesh Chandra Ghosh would reconvey the land of the aforementioned kabalas, that Manada Chandra Ghosh paid back the loan amount to Nagesh Chandra Ghosh and he executed a deed of re-conveyance on July 14, 1964 but the deed of re-conveyance could not be registered because of the provision of Ordinance No. 1 of 1964, that on execution of the deed of re-conveyance possession of the land in suit was surrendered by Nagesh chandra Ghosh to Manada Chandra Ghosh and he since the date of deed of re-conveyance possessed the land on payment of rent to the Government, that Manada Chandra Ghosh possessed the land to the knowledge of every body including Nagesh Chandra Ghosh, that Manada Chandra Ghosh died leaving son by name Madan Chandra Ghosh and wife Parul Bala and they possessed the land in suit, that Madan Chandra Ghosh and Parul Bala sold the land in suit to the plaintiff by the kabala dated January 31, 1985 and made over possession of the land so sold and the plaintiffs are in possession of the land since their purchase, that after purchase when the plaintiffs took steps for mutation of their names it was noticed that defendant No.1 illegally mutated his name in respect of the part of the land in suit and the plaintiffs as against the mutation filed objection and the same was allowed, that thereafter plaintiffs came to know that defendant No.1 in collusion with the defendant No.2 obtained two kabalas dated March 17, 1983 and March 28, 1983 in respect of the land in suit, that plaintiffs further came to know that defendant No.3 executed a kabala in favour of defendant No.5 on December 13, 1989 in respect of the land in suit, that after re-conveyance predecessor of plaintiffs vendor possessed the land in suit in assertion of his right and after him plaintiffs' vendors possessed the land in question of their right and adversely against all including the defendants over the statutory period of limitation prior to the selling of the land to the plaintiffs and plaintiffs' vendor inducted the plaintiffs into possession of land in suit, that the plaintiffs have acquired title in the land in suit by purchase as well as by adverse possession, that as the kabalas of the defendant Nos.1 and 5 have created cloud on the title of the plaintiffs, they are constrained to file the suit.

4. The suit was contested by the defendant Nos.1 and 5 stating, inter alia, that Manda Chandra Ghosh took loan from Nagesh Chandra Ghosh and executed two deeds on August 1, 1962 and August 3, 1962 and that while Nagesh Chandra Ghosh was in possession he died leaving defendant Nos. 2 and 3 as heirs and defendant No.2 sold his share to defendant No.1 on March 17, 1985 and defendant No.3 sold his share to defendant No.5 on December 13, 1989 and put them into possession and the defendants in the aforesaid manner are in possession of the land in suit, that after death of Manada Chandra Ghosh his son Madan Chandra Ghosh and his wife Parul Bala brought Redemption Case No. 30 of 1973 before the Revenue Officer and the Revenue Officer rejected the same and as against that no further step was taken with regard to the Ekrarnama dated August 14, 1962 and the kabala dated January 31, 1985 is collusive and forged, that the plaintiffs and their vendors have and had no right, title and interest in the land in suit.

5. The trial court decreed the suit on the finding that the plaintiff were successful in establishing their case by oral and documentary evidence. The contesting defendants went on appeal. The appellate Court on consideration of the land in suit is being possessed by the plaintiffs through their vendors since July 14, 1964 "in exclusion of and within the knowledge of the defendant-appellants and their predecessors on the basis of the invalid document Ext. 2.......Since then the plaintiff-respondents appear to have possessing through their predecessors without any interruption till the 1st part of July, 1986. In this view of the matter their possession over the suit land appears to be for more than 12 years without any interruption".

6. The defendants moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained the Rule. The High Court Division on consideration of the documentary as well as oral evidence held "the documentary evidence such as exhibit-2, return deed read with exhibit-6(ka) proved that Manada had been in possession of the suit land after his death his heirs Madan and defendant No.3 Parul Bala were in possession of the suit land" and thereafter plaintiffs are in possession of the land in suit.

<u>7. We have heard the learned Advocate and perused the materials in the petition for leave to appeal. From the judgment of the High Court Division as well as of the Courts below it is seen that possession of the plaintiffs and prior to the their vendors for more than statutory period of limitation for acquiring title has been established by documentary as well as by oral evidence.</u>

8. The learned Advocate could not point out any infirmity of the kind in the judgment of the High Court Division calling for interference.

9. Accordingly the petition is dismissed.

End.
